chunks: Alaa ibn Rabee' narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The testimony of a Muslim slave is valid against a Muslim free man.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: All these narrations have come down, with an addition regarding the permissibility of accepting the testimony of slaves, and there has also come down that which prevents this, some of which we have previously mentioned in the narration of Sama'ah, and some of which he narrated.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a Muslim slave valid against a free man in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirms the general legal validity of a Muslim slave's testimony against a free man, reflecting the principle that social status does not inherently invalidate judicial witness. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by noting that while this ruling stands, it coexists with other narrations—such as the case of Sama'ah—that impose specific restrictions on the testimony of slaves, illustrating the nuanced interplay between general principles and specific exceptions in Shia fiqh.
